extension_of_upstream: Large size only. Upstream's default vector length is 64 and its preset lengths are 4096, 65536, and 131072; this port runs 1,048,576 elements (the element count of the legacy standalone vec_add.cu) with upstream's default multiplier 2 and bias 0. The kernel semantics are unchanged.

sources.role: input generation, the element-wise int32 add, and the host result and checksum check
build options (-ffp-contract=off) and the smoke and validation settings

data_generation.inputs: No inputs are read. For index i = 0 .. length-1: lhs[i] = i and rhs[i] = i * multiplier + bias, both int32. The upstream defaults are multiplier 2 and bias 0, which this port keeps for the large workload.
data_generation.semantics: result[i] = lhs[i] + rhs[i] in int32, so result[i] = i * (multiplier + 1) + bias. The 64-bit checksum is the sum of every result element accumulated in a signed 64-bit integer; for the large workload it is 3 * N * (N - 1) / 2 = 1,649,265,868,800. The oracle computes it, nothing hardcodes it.
data_generation.validity: length must be at least 1 and at most 2^27, multiplier and bias must fit int32, and every lhs, rhs, and result value must fit int32 (the values are linear in i, so the extremes are at i = 0 and i = length-1, checked in 128-bit arithmetic); anything else exits 2 with a message. Upstream has no such guard because its sizes are fixed; the checks keep the int32 arithmetic free of signed overflow.

outputs.name: result
outputs.layout: little-endian int32, indexed by element, as downloaded to pinned host memory; the digest is FNV-1a 64 over these bytes

outputs.name: checksum
outputs.layout: host-side sum of the downloaded result elements, compared with the oracle's checksum; not a device output

result.comparison: exact integer equality for every element
result.source: private Loom's vecadd_memory.c returns failure when any result differs from i * (multiplier + 1) + bias
result.oracle: oracle.cpp: an independent host loop that builds both inputs in 64-bit arithmetic and adds them

checksum.source: the checksum private Loom's vecadd_memory.c prints on the host and its expected-*.txt oracles record

tolerances.cross_invocation: two Direct and two Graph invocations must produce bitwise-identical results

timing_scope.application: upload of lhs and rhs from pinned host memory, the element-wise add, and download of result to pinned host memory
timing_scope.compute: the element-wise add with lhs and rhs resident on the device; no transfers
timing_scope.excluded: input generation, allocation, CUDA Graph construction, warmups, the CPU oracle, and output checking
